shortcut_name: Steiner routing through intermediate support platforms
evidence: "Floyd-Warshall" followed by subset-based processing; "full = (1 << t) - 1" and "dp = [[INF] * n ...]"
affordance_in_statement: The remaining platforms are structural supports: you may route cables through them if it minimizes total expenditure, or bypass them entirely.
secondary_shortcut_name: small terminal set enabling subset dynamic programming
removal_suggestion: None without changing the task: permitting non-primary platforms as shared routing junctions is the defining Steiner-tree structure. Rephrasing it can hide the idea but cannot remove the underlying affordance.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Recognizes the problem as a Steiner tree and uses all-pairs shortest paths before subset processing.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The remaining platforms ... may route cables through them if it minimizes total expenditure

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Uses the small-terminal subset DP formulation of the Steiner tree problem.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: all primary turbine platforms are integrated into a single continuous grid ... directly or through intermediate platforms

common_affordance: Allowing arbitrary non-terminal platforms to serve as intermediate shared routing vertices

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: Builds an MST over terminals using shortest-path distances, which cannot account for one shared Steiner support being cheaper than the terminal metric MST.
Explicitly implements a Steiner tree approximation rather than the required exact optimization, so it can miss the minimum-cost shared-support network.

recommended_edit: No semantics-preserving edit can defeat both surviving solutions: the common affordance is the core optimization structure of the problem. Any edit that disallows or restricts intermediate support platforms changes the task from Steiner-tree connectivity to a different problem.
